stem: In a child with suspected inhaled foreign body, what abnormality are inspiratory and expiratory chest radiographs mainly intended to assess?
explanation: Air trapping is the main abnormality assessed on inspiratory and expiratory chest radiographs when an inhaled foreign body is suspected.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because expiratory films can show unilateral or focal air trapping from partial airway obstruction by an inhaled foreign body.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pleural effusion is not the main target of inspiratory and expiratory views in suspected airway foreign body.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because cardiomegaly is not what these views are used to assess in this setting.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because free subdiaphragmatic gas is assessed on abdominal or erect chest imaging for perforation, not foreign body air trapping.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because skull fracture is unrelated to chest radiography for a suspected inhaled foreign body.
